briefings.title: Christine Lagarde on the New Global Order
briefings.tldr: Speaking at the 2026 New York Times DealBook Summit, European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde argued that global trust is in short supply—prompting her decision to step down from the ECB nine months early to speak freely on non-monetary issues—while emphasizing that AI-driven supply chains have kept global trade growing despite tariffs and geopolitical tensions.

briefings.title: Palmer Luckey on War 2.0
briefings.tldr: In a wide-ranging interview with Andrew Ross Sorkin at the 2026 DealBook Summit, Anduril Industries founder Palmer Luckey argued that the U.S. must overhaul its military and technological posture—from renaming the Pentagon to the Department of War and restarting nuclear EMP testing to building offshore industrial platforms—while warning that rapid AI-driven cyber exploits are outpacing legacy defenses.

briefings.title: Satya Nadella on the New Algorithm
briefings.tldr: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the company’s $175 billion AI infrastructure push, arguing that Microsoft is playing a "model system" game—commoditizing AI tokens via Copilot and its own cost-efficient M.A.I. models while maintaining a royalty-free OpenAI partnership through 2032.

briefings.title: Elon Musk Says He’s ‘Not MAGA’
briefings.tldr: At the 2026 New York Times DealBook Summit, Elon Musk—interviewed by Andrew Ross Sorkin—addressed his political spending and rejection of the "MAGA" label, defended his refusal to allow commercial Starlink to be used for offensive military strikes in Ukraine, and outlined how AI and robotics are driving convergence between SpaceX and Tesla.

briefings.title: Why Sam Altman and Greg Brockman Say Humans Must Stay in Control of AI
briefings.tldr: OpenAI co-founders Sam Altman and Greg Brockman emphasized that humans must remain in control of AI's future, arguing that technical alignment and industry-wide safety standards must scale alongside rapidly advancing capabilities.
